title: win-sshproxy fails with WSAEADDRINUSE (bind: Only one usage of each socket address is normally permitted) when restarting Podman machine on Windows
body:
### Issue Description
On Windows, when starting a Podman machine (`podman machine start`) after a previous shutdown, reboot, or non-clean termination, `win-sshproxy.exe` fails to start with the following error logged in Windows Event Viewer:

```
[error] podman-machine-default: Error occurred in execution group: error listening on socket: /%TEMP%/podman/podman-machine-default-api.sock: listen unix %TEMP%/podman/podman-machine-default-api.sock: bind: Only one usage of each socket address (protocol/network address/port) is normally permitted.
```

As a result, `podman machine start` fails or the API forwarding proxy exits immediately.

### Root Cause
Unlike Linux, where Go's `net.Listen("unix", path)` removes/unlinks dead/stale socket files automatically, on Windows (Winsock `AF_UNIX`), if the `.sock` file already exists on the filesystem from a previous run, `bind()` fails with `WSAEADDRINUSE` (error code 10048).

In `win-sshproxy` (within `containers/gvisor-tap-vsock` / `containers/podman`), `net.Listen("unix", path)` is called without first unlinking/deleting any leftover socket file at that path.

### Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Run `podman machine start` (first start succeeds and creates `%TEMP%\podman\podman-machine-default-api.sock`).
2. Stop the machine or restart Windows without manual cleanup.
3. Observe that `%TEMP%\podman\podman-machine-default-api.sock` (0 bytes) remains on disk.
4. Run `podman machine start` again.
5. `win-sshproxy` fails with `bind: Only one usage of each socket address (protocol/network address/port) is normally permitted.`

### Describe the results you received
`podman machine start` fails with WSAEADDRINUSE error from `win-sshproxy.exe`.

### Describe the results you expected
`win-sshproxy.exe` should either remove/unlink any existing stale `.sock` file prior to calling `net.Listen("unix", path)` or overwrite it, allowing the machine to start normally across restarts.

### podman info output
```yaml

  Built: 1791838521
  BuiltTime: Mon Oct 12 23:55:21 2026
  GitCommit: 464c15fec06f0074c916f9eff87c4806869c2833
  GoVersion: go1.26.8
  Os: windows
  OsArch: windows/amd64

  kernel: 6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2
  networkBackend: netavark
  ociRuntime:

  serviceIsRemote: true

  Built: 1791763200
  GitCommit: 464c15fec06f0074c916f9eff87c4806869c2833

```

### Podman in a container
No

### Privileged Or Rootless
Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release
Yes

### Additional environment details
Windows 11 / Windows 10 (WSL2 / Hyper-V backend)
Podman 6.1.4 release for Windows

### Additional information
**Workaround:**
Deleting stale `.sock` files in `%TEMP%\podman\` prior to startup resolves the problem:
```powershell
Remove-Item "$env:TEMP\podman\*.sock" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
podman machine start
```

**Proposed Fix in Go:**
Before calling `net.Listen("unix", path)` on Windows:
```go
_ = os.Remove(path)
listener, err := net.Listen("unix", path)
```

comments.body:
> Unlike Linux, where Go's net.Listen("unix", path) removes/unlinks dead/stale socket files automatically, on Windows (Winsock AF_UNIX), if the .sock file already exists on the filesystem from a previous run, bind() fails with WSAEADDRINUSE (error code 10048).

That makes no sense to me, on linux/macos a leftover socket file will always fail with `address already in use` as well.
What Go does is to delete the file on Close by default. But of course on a non clean termination that will not happen and then the file is leaked. So of course we need to clean it up ourself on start again.

The only question is should we delete the `win-sshproxy` socket path on the podman or win-sshproxy side?
cc @cfergeau @l0rd

There are some code paths in gvisor-tap-vsock where we do not want to remove the socket file before listening, so I’d prefer to never remove socket files. If this is too strict and causes too many problems, we’ll consider removing the socket files which are passed on `win-sshproxy`/`gvproxy` command line before `Listen`, this should be relatively harmless.
As you pointed out, regardless of what we do, code will be needed in podman for non-clean termination.

I also need to check if socket files are cleaned up on clean 'win-sshproxy' shutdown, if not this would be a bug we need to fix in `win-sshproxy`

> If this is too strict and causes too many problems, we’ll consider removing the socket files which are passed on win-sshproxy/gvproxy command line before Listen, this should be relatively harmless.
As you pointed out, regardless of what we do, code will be needed in podman for non-clean termination.

Yeah I understand your concern but cli arguments should be trusted, but I certainly understand the argument of the process does not know if the existing socket is still in use. Doing the removal on the podman side only would be fine with me. 

> I also need to check if socket files are cleaned up on clean 'win-sshproxy' shutdown, if not this would be a bug we need to fix in win-sshproxy

The go std libary removes the file as long as you call Close() on the listener before program exit.

>         > I also need to check if socket files are cleaned up on clean 'win-sshproxy' shutdown, if not this would be a bug we need to fix in win-sshproxy
>             
>         The go std libary removes the file as long as you call Close() on the listener before program exit.

`win-sshproxy` apparently does the right thing from that perspective, but since there is this bug report, I prefer to carry out more extensive testing in case I misread the code.

I'm hitting this too, and can add a data point for @cfergeau's question about clean shutdowns.

**Environment:** Podman 6.1.4 (Windows client), Windows 11, WSL provider, rootful machine, Podman Desktop 1.30.5.

**What happened:** I rebooted Windows while the machine was running. On the next `podman machine start`, the CLI printed `win-sshproxy.exe failed to start, exit code: 0 (see windows event logs)`, but still ended with "started successfully". The Event Viewer entry matches this issue exactly:

```
[error] podman-machine-default: Error occurred in execution group: error listening on socket: .../Temp/podman/podman-machine-default-api.sock: listen unix ...: bind: Only one usage of each socket address (protocol/network address/port) is normally permitted.
```

The same log shows `win-sshproxy` listening on both `\\.\pipe\podman-machine-default` and `\\.\pipe\docker_engine` right before this error. The process then exits, so both pipes disappear. The CLI keeps working over SSH, but Podman Desktop and Docker API clients lose API forwarding. Podman Desktop showed no containers, images or volumes (`connect ENOENT \\.\pipe\podman-machine-default`).

**Clean shutdown:** for me, `podman machine stop` removes `podman-machine-default-api.sock`, so the leak only seems to happen on a non-clean exit such as a reboot with the machine running.

**Workaround:** with the machine stopped, deleting that one stale file makes `podman machine start` work and Podman Desktop shows my data again.

This worked for me on earlier version 6 without any manual step (I could reboot with the machine running), so a cleanup on start in Podman, as discussed above, would fix it.

Hitting this too, with two extra data points that may matter for the fix.

**Environment:** Podman 6.1.4 (Windows client), Windows 11 Enterprise 26200, WSL provider, rootful machine, Podman Desktop 1.30.5.

**Symptom:** Podman Desktop showed no containers while `podman ps -a` listed all of them. `\\.\pipe\podman-machine-default` and `\\.\pipe\docker_engine` did not exist and no `win-sshproxy.exe` was running. The stale `%TEMP%\podman\podman-machine-default-api.sock` (0 bytes) dated from the previous day.

### 1. A clean stop/start does not help, and the bind error changes

The first failure (the first machine start of the day) logged the same error as this issue:

```
bind: Only one usage of each socket address (protocol/network address/port) is normally permitted.
```

After a clean `podman machine stop` / `podman machine start`, with no `win-sshproxy.exe` or `gvproxy.exe` running, it still failed, but with a different error:

```
[error] podman-machine-default: Error occurred in execution group: error listening on socket: /C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Temp/podman/podman-machine-default-api.sock: listen unix C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Temp/podman/podman-machine-default-api.sock: bind: An invalid argument was supplied.
```

So anyone searching for `WSAEADDRINUSE` alone may miss this one. In both cases the CLI prints `win-sshproxy.exe failed to start, exit code: 0` and then `started successfully`.

### 2. The stale socket file cannot be deleted directly

With the machine stopped, every way I tried to delete the file failed:

| Method | Result |
|---|---|
| `Remove-Item -Force` | `The file cannot be accessed by the system.` |
| `cmd /c del /f /q` | `The file cannot be accessed by the system.` |
| `fsutil reparsepoint delete` | `Error 1920: The file cannot be accessed by the system.` |
| `[System.IO.File]::Delete()` | `The file cannot be accessed by the system.` |

What worked was renaming the parent folder (`%TEMP%\podman` to `%TEMP%\podman.stale-<timestamp>`) and then running `podman machine start`. After that, `win-sshproxy` started, both pipes came back, and Podman Desktop saw the containers again.

If the fix removes the socket file before `Listen`, it may hit the same error on some systems. A fallback such as renaming the file (or its directory) could be needed, or a log message that tells the user what to remove manually.

**Workaround for others:**

```powershell
podman machine stop
Rename-Item "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Temp\podman" "podman.stale-$(Get-Date -f yyyyMMddHHmmss)"
podman machine start
```

#29985 looks like the same root cause (WSL, 6.1.4, proxy exits with code 0, no pipe).

This is fixed in the main branch https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29765

On main branch, on `podman machine start`, we check if 1) the pipe is in use 2) the file `win-sshproxy.tid` exists. When both conditions are met, we kill the corresponding process and, after checking that the pipe is no longer in use, start `win-sshproxy`. I don't think we need to delete the socket.

But there are a few open questions:
- previously (v6.1.3) this wasn't a big deal on WSL: `podman machine start` reported the error `could not start api proxy`, but the pre-existing `win-sshproxy` was still working and forwarding `podman commands`. It looks like with v6.1.4 it no longer works.
- the workaround described in this issue, removing the .sock file, should not fix `podman machine start`. After removing the UNIX socket, the leftover win-sshproxy will still be listening to the pipe `\\\\.\\pipe\\podman-machine-default`, and `podman machine start` should still report the same error

I want to investigate these before closing this issue.

And I found another, more subtle bug related to that: `wsl --shutdown` (non-clean machine termination), followed by a `podman machine rm/reset`, deletes `win-sshproxy.tid` without stopping the process. Then the next `podman machine start` fails because it can't find the `win-sshproxy` tid. I am preparing a PR to fix that too.
